title: Reach a Number
statement:
You start at `0` on a number line that extends forever in both directions and want to land exactly on the integer `target`. Moves are numbered from `1`: move number `i` carries you exactly `i` units, and before each move you choose whether to go left or right.

Return the smallest number of moves after which you can be standing on `target`.
notes:
## Intuition

Left and right are mirror images, so only `goal = |target|` matters. A search over all left/right choices doubles with every move, so instead think about walking right every time: after `k` moves you stand at `1 + 2 + ... + k`. Turning move `i` around lowers that total by `2i`, so flipping moves can only remove an **even** amount. Every whole number from `0` up to the total can be written as a sum of distinct moves, so any even surplus `d` can be removed by flipping moves that add up to `d / 2`. The answer is therefore the first `k` whose total reaches `goal` with an even surplus.

## Approach

1. Set `goal` to `|target|`.
2. Solve `k(k + 1) / 2 >= goal` in closed form for the smallest such `moves`, and compute its total `sum`.
3. While `sum` is short of `goal` or `sum - goal` is odd, take one more move and add it to `sum`.
4. Return `moves`. At most two extra moves are ever needed, because among the next two moves at least one is odd and flips the parity.

## Example 1, step by step

`target = 2`, so `goal = 2`. The formula gives `moves = ceil((sqrt(17) - 1) / 2) = 2` and `sum = 3`. The surplus `3 - 2 = 1` is odd, so take move 3: `sum = 6`, surplus `4`, which is even. Return `3`: flipping move 2 (half of the surplus) gives `1 - 2 + 3 = 2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1): one square root plus at most two loop rounds.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Use `Math.abs(target)`; a negative target needs exactly as many moves as its mirror.
- Reaching `goal` is not enough: an odd surplus cannot be removed by flipping, so keep moving.
- Stopping on the first total of at least `goal` without checking parity returns too small an answer (for example `2` instead of `3` for `target = 2`).

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `goal` | distance to cover, `|target|` |
| `moves` | number of moves taken so far |
| `sum` | position after walking right on every move, `1 + 2 + ... + moves` |

narration.2: Left and right are symmetric, so only the distance to the target matters.
narration.3: Solve k(k + 1) / 2 >= goal for the fewest moves whose all-right total reaches the goal.
narration.4: The position reached by walking right on every one of those moves.
narration.6: Keep moving while the total falls short or the surplus is odd, since flipping a move changes the total by an even amount.
narration.8: ...and walk it to the right as well.
narration.10: The surplus is now even, so flipping moves worth half of it lands exactly on the target.
